# (PART) Reference {-}

# Theory Atlas {#theory-atlas}

The Theory Atlas collects every entry in the book in one place. Use it to look up
a theory's core claim, find theories that operate through the same mechanism, or
locate candidates for a research question. In the online edition the table is
searchable, sortable, and filterable; each theory name links to its full entry.

```{r atlas-data}
atlas <- readr::read_csv("data/theory-atlas.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
# bs4_book writes one page per chapter, named after the chapter id.
chapter_page <- c("intro", "what-is-theory", "using-theory", "resources", "dynamic-capabilities",
                  "governance", "environment", "information", "networks-exchange",
                  "innovation-adoption", "culture", "motivation", "self-regulation",
                  "social-influence", "judgment-decision", "emotion-wellbeing",
                  "persuasion-communication", "effects", "phenomena", "frameworks")
atlas$href <- paste0(chapter_page[atlas$chapter], ".html#", atlas$anchor)
```

## Searchable atlas {#atlas-table}

```{r tab-atlas-full}
if (is_html()) {
  atlas |>
    dplyr::arrange(chapter, theory) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      Theory = sprintf('<a href="%s">%s</a>', href, htmltools::htmlEscape(theory)),
      Ch. = chapter, Part = part, Mechanism = mechanism, Level = level,
      `Key source` = key_source, `Core claim` = core_claim, `Business use` = business_use,
      Discipline = discipline
    ) |>
    DT::datatable(
      escape = FALSE, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
      extensions = c("Buttons", "Responsive"),
      caption = "The Theory Atlas: every entry in the book.",
      options = list(pageLength = 15, autoWidth = FALSE, dom = "Bfrtip",
                     buttons = c("copy", "csv"),
                     columnDefs = list(list(visible = FALSE, targets = 8)),
                     order = list(list(1, "asc")))
    )
} else {
  atlas |>
    dplyr::arrange(chapter, theory) |>
    dplyr::select(Theory = theory, Ch. = chapter, Mechanism = mechanism, `Key source` = key_source) |>
    book_table(caption = "The Theory Atlas: every entry in the book.", font_size = 9)
}
```

The atlas is also available as a plain CSV file,
[`data/theory-atlas.csv`](https://github.com/mikenguyen13/social-theory/blob/master/data/theory-atlas.csv),
for use in teaching materials, literature reviews, or your own analyses.

## Theories by mechanism {#atlas-mechanisms}

Theories that share a mechanism are natural competitors or complements. Figure
\@ref(fig:fig-atlas-mech) counts the entries by dominant mechanism and part of the
book.

```{r fig-atlas-mech, fig.cap = "Entries in the book by dominant mechanism, stacked by part of the book.", fig.height = 5.4}
part_levels <- c("Foundations", "Organizations & Strategy", "Individuals & Groups",
                 "Effects, Phenomena & Frameworks")
mech <- atlas |>
  dplyr::count(mechanism, part) |>
  dplyr::mutate(part = factor(part, levels = part_levels))
ord <- mech |> dplyr::group_by(mechanism) |> dplyr::summarise(t = sum(n)) |> dplyr::arrange(t)
mech$mechanism <- factor(mech$mechanism, levels = ord$mechanism)
ggplot(mech, aes(n, mechanism, fill = part)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(unname(pal[c("violet", "blue", "orange", "aqua")]), part_levels),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Number of entries", y = NULL, title = "Which mechanisms do the theories rely on?") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "top") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

```{r tab-atlas-mechanisms}
mech_desc <- tibble::tribble(
  ~mechanism, ~`What drives behaviour`,
  "Information", "What actors know, can observe, or can infer from others' actions",
  "Incentives", "Payoffs, contracts, and the costs of transacting",
  "Resources & capabilities", "Heterogeneous, hard-to-imitate assets and routines",
  "Learning & adaptation", "Search, experimentation, selection, and reconfiguration",
  "Power & dependence", "Control over resources that others need",
  "Legitimacy & institutions", "Taken-for-granted rules, norms, and social approval",
  "Networks & exchange", "Relationships, reciprocity, and positions in social structure",
  "Diffusion & adoption", "Spread of practices and technologies through social systems",
  "Culture & values", "Shared values and norms that differ across societies",
  "Motivation & goals", "Goals, expectations, rewards, and self-regulation",
  "Identity & social comparison", "Who people think they are and how they compare with others",
  "Cognition & heuristics", "Limited attention, mental shortcuts, and representation",
  "Emotion & affect", "Feelings, arousal, and their influence on judgment",
  "Explanation", "Meta-theoretical tools for building and testing theory"
)
atlas |>
  dplyr::group_by(mechanism) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Entries = dplyr::n(),
                   Examples = paste(head(theory, 4), collapse = "; ")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(mech_desc, by = "mechanism") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Entries)) |>
  dplyr::select(Mechanism = mechanism, `What drives behaviour`, Entries, Examples) |>
  book_table(caption = "Mechanism families used in the atlas.")
```

## Glossary {#glossary}

```{r tab-glossary}
tibble::tribble(
  ~Term, ~Definition,
  "Adverse selection", "A hidden-information problem in which the parties most eager to transact are those the other side would least want to transact with.",
  "Boundary condition", "A limit on the who, where, and when to which a theory's predictions apply.",
  "Construct", "An abstract concept (e.g., trust, legitimacy) that a theory relates to other concepts; measured imperfectly by variables.",
  "Countersignaling", "Deliberately not sending a signal because other information already separates the sender from low types.",
  "Descriptive norm", "Perception of what most people actually do.",
  "Dynamic capability", "A firm's ability to integrate, build, and reconfigure competences to address changing environments.",
  "Equilibrium (pooling)", "An outcome in which different types take the same action, so the action reveals nothing.",
  "Equilibrium (separating)", "An outcome in which different types take different actions, so the action reveals type.",
  "HARKing", "Hypothesizing after the results are known: presenting post hoc hypotheses as if they were a priori.",
  "Injunctive norm", "Perception of what most people approve or disapprove of.",
  "Isomorphism", "The tendency of organizations in a field to become similar in structure and practice.",
  "Level of analysis", "The unit (individual, dyad, group, firm, market) at which a construct or theory is defined.",
  "Loss aversion", "The tendency for losses to loom larger than gains of the same size.",
  "Mechanism", "The process through which a cause produces an effect; the 'why' of a theory.",
  "Mediator", "A variable that transmits the effect of an independent variable to a dependent variable.",
  "Moderator", "A variable that changes the strength or direction of a relationship.",
  "Moral hazard", "A hidden-action problem in which one party changes behaviour after a contract because the other cannot observe it.",
  "Nomological network", "The web of theoretical relationships in which a construct is embedded, used to establish construct validity.",
  "Proposition", "A statement of relationship between constructs; a hypothesis is its testable counterpart in terms of variables.",
  "Reference point", "The benchmark against which outcomes are coded as gains or losses.",
  "Regulatory fit", "The increased value people experience when the manner of goal pursuit matches their regulatory orientation.",
  "Signal", "An observable action chosen by an informed party that conveys information about an unobservable characteristic.",
  "Social capital", "Resources embedded in, and accessible through, social relationships.",
  "Structural hole", "A gap between two contacts who are not connected to each other, which a broker can span.",
  "VRIO", "Valuable, rare, inimitable, organized: the conditions for a resource to yield sustained competitive advantage."
) |>
  book_table(caption = "Glossary of recurring terms.")
```
